MIXES.who: Pothos, peperomia, spider plant, syngonium, aglaonema, ZZ, ferns
MIXES.nt: What the bag was made for. Add nothing.

MIXES.who: Any of the above in a plastic pot, or anything potted during monsoon
MIXES.nt: A little perlite is cheap insurance against a pot that never dries.

MIXES.who: Jade, echeveria, haworthia, sedum, graptoveria — most succulents
MIXES.nt: Your jade needs this. Neat Magic Soil will rot it within a season.

MIXES.who: Cactus, adenium, lithops, euphorbia, caudex plants
MIXES.nt: Mostly mineral. Finished mix should pour through your fingers, not clump.

MIXES.who: Turmeric and gingers, chilli, curry leaf, lemongrass, dwarf fruit trees
MIXES.nt: If the tall ones smell of ginger when crushed, they belong in this.

MIXES.who: Rooting cuttings, seed trays, tiny plugs
MIXES.nt: No vermicompost — fresh roots burn on it.
No Magic Soil at all. Orchid roots need air and will drown in it.

POTTYPES: The default, and the safest choice while your light is poor. Can cook roots in a sunny window.
Best pot there is for jade and succulents. In May it can dry a small pot in a day — watch it.
Heavy and handsome. Check it has a real drainage hole before you buy.
For gingers, turmeric, chilli and anything that sends roots straight down.
Dries evenly, no soggy bottom. Succulent arrangements, bonsai, lithops.
Excellent roots, cheap, folds away. Drips everywhere — stand it in a solid tray on your tiles.
Useful if you travel. Never for succulents, and risky until you can read a plant well.
Bark only. Water by dunking, not pouring.

BAGTYPES.root: Air-prunes — roots stop at the wall and branch. No circling.
BAGTYPES.verdict: Use this. 400 GSM, beige or grey or white only.

BAGTYPES.root: Roots circle and girdle. Mandatory root-prune every two years.
BAGTYPES.verdict: Fine for the temporary intermediate size, or until the drip line runs — it holds water longer.

BAGTYPES.n: Black plastic pot or poly bag
BAGTYPES.verdict: Never. Cooks the fine feeder roots while the leaves still look perfectly fine.

BAGTYPES.root: Fine. Evaporative cooling through the wall.
BAGTYPES.verdict: Good final home for mango and sapota if you can accept the weight.

parts: Coco peat, charged, or leaf mould
Coarse river sand or 4–6 mm grit
am: potash and calcium — skip if pH is already above 7.5

soft.name: Soft mix
soft.for: Brinjal, chilli, and every vegetable bag
am: calcium — this is what prevents blossom end rot

seed.name: Seed-starting mix
parts: Coco peat, charged and sieved fine
